name: Differentiating under the integral sign
statement: If a parameter-dependent integrand and its partial derivative in the parameter are continuous on a rectangle, then the parameter integral is differentiable and its derivative is the integral of the partial derivative.
conditions: f(x,t) and partial f/partial x are continuous on D={(x,t): a <= x <= b, c <= t <= d}.
F(x)=integral_c^d f(x,t) dt.
conclusion: F is differentiable on [a,b] and F'(x)=integral_c^d partial f/partial x (x,t) dt.
typical_uses: Repair parameter integral derivative computations.
Justify moving derivatives through finite integrals.
common_misuses: Differentiating under the integral sign without continuity or domination hypotheses.
Confusing derivative with respect to x and integration variable t.
bridge_lemmas: Uniform continuity of the partial derivative on the compact rectangle controls difference quotients uniformly in t.
repair_templates: Verify continuity of both f and f_x on the whole rectangle before interchanging derivative and integral.

name: Improper integral Cauchy and comparison tests
statement: An improper integral over an infinite interval converges exactly when far tails are Cauchy; nonnegative integrands obey comparison and absolute convergence tests.
conditions: f is Riemann integrable on [a,b] for every finite b >= a.
For comparison, 0 <= f(t) <= g(t) eventually.
conclusion: Integral_a^infinity f converges iff for every epsilon > 0 there exists M such that y>x>=M implies |integral_x^y f|<epsilon; if 0<=f<=g and integral g converges then integral f converges; absolute convergence implies convergence.
typical_uses: Repair convergence proofs for improper integrals.
Transfer series-test intuition to integrals.
common_misuses: Checking only that f(t)->0.
Using comparison with the inequality in the wrong direction.
bridge_lemmas: Apply the Cauchy criterion to F(b)=integral_a^b f.
repair_templates: Estimate arbitrary far-tail integrals, or dominate the absolute value by a known convergent improper integral.

name: Riemann-Lebesgue lemma
statement: The integral of a continuous function against high-frequency sine or cosine tends to zero.
conditions: h is continuous on a bounded interval such as [-pi,pi].
conclusion: integral h(x) sin(nx) dx -> 0 and integral h(x) cos(nx) dx -> 0 as n -> infinity, over the fixed interval.
typical_uses: Prove convergence facts for Fourier coefficients and Fourier series.
Repair arguments involving oscillatory integrals.
common_misuses: Applying the lemma without integrability or continuity-type hypotheses.
Assuming pointwise convergence of integrands is enough without oscillation control.
bridge_lemmas: Uniform continuity lets nearby half-period contributions nearly cancel.
repair_templates: Partition into intervals adapted to the oscillation period and use uniform continuity to bound cancellations.

name: Fejer theorem
statement: For a continuous periodic function, the Cesaro means of its Fourier partial sums converge uniformly to the function.
conditions: f is continuous on (-pi,pi] with f(-pi)=f(pi) under the periodic interpretation.
sigma_N is the average of the first N Fourier partial sums.
conclusion: sigma_N -> f uniformly.
typical_uses: Recover continuous functions by averaged Fourier sums.

common_misuses: Confusing convergence of Fourier partial sums with convergence of their Cesaro means.
Ignoring periodic endpoint matching.
bridge_lemmas: The Fejer kernel is nonnegative, integrates to one, and concentrates near zero.
